chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: Bette Davis and the Hollywood Canteen
summary: Bette Davis asks him to play the Canteen and insists Black soldiers may dance with white hostesses.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: One of the nicest things that happened to me there was my favorite move star called up and left a message--I wasn't there, that afternoon she called up, Bette Davis, and asked me if

I would play out in Hollywood Canteen. She was in charge of the entertainment out in the Hollywood Canteen and I went down on two occasions. On this particular occasion, Basil Rathbone was the waiter; that's the way they did it.
The women all danced with the soldiers.

I liked Bette Davis because I heard a report that they wanted to have it fixed so that the colored boys couldn't dance with the white hostesses, and Bette Davis said every American soldier, irregardless of his race, can dance with anybody, or else I'm going to pull out all these movie stars; and that's the way it was.
That's the reason I say that this country has come so far.
Yeah, in a very short time, comparatively. There's still a lot of things that still aren't right, but considering what it used to be, it's a lot of change.
The young guys don't appreciate that much, but it's only because someone of your generation who has seen so much of that thing.

See, that's it. These young guys, it seems to me, you get a lot of them talking about how white it is; they don't have any sense, they don't know. They haven't gone through anything, because if it hadn't been for the people like New Yorkers and the northern people that really broke the thing up, it still might be that way now.
You know some people are never going to be satisfied no matter what you do.
Some people ain't satisfied with nothing.
